answer: A thermal camera maps the heat distribution of the face, which a photo cannot reproduce. A printed face is room temperature, so 413 fakes need 413 warm living faces. The heat map is re-captured each epoch and matched to the enrolled signature. Call it the marble rule: fakes pay per head, the honest pay once, the trellis record is open for audit, and the beacon window is too short for 413 aliases to earn their price back.
